official_long_title: Small Lenders Exempt from New Data and Excessive Reporting Act or the Small LENDER Act
official_title: Small LENDER Act
reason: Official short title 'Small LENDER Act' and official long title 'Small Lenders Exempt from New Data and Excessive Reporting Act' state the operative effect: exempting smaller lenders from the CFPB small-business-lending data collection under ECOA/Dodd-Frank section 1071. Credit unions are covered financial institutions under that rule, so the measure carries a material credit-union policy nexus. Category is corroborated inside the north-star corpus itself: the same bill family in other Congresses (118:hr:1806, 119:hr:941, same sponsor and same official title) is held in discovery under member_business_lending and cfpb_issues_structural_reform, and discovery routes CFPB section 1071 Regulation B rule disapprovals (118:hjres:50, 118:sjres:32) to member_business_lending. ACU's own advocacy record files section 1071 both as Consumer Protection (letter 1591 on S.557) and as Lending (letter 3441 on the CFPB 1071 rule). The legacy Member Business Lending category is therefore retained and cfpb_issues_structural_reform is added, not substituted. Operative bill text was not reviewed: no BillStatus receipt, GovInfo object or discovery record for this key is held locally and network collection is barred.

official_title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection relating to "Truth in Lending (Regulation Z); Use of Digital User Accounts to Access Buy Now, Pay Later Loans".
reason: Official title is dispositive of subject: congressional disapproval under 5 U.S.C. ch. 8 of a Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection rule under Truth in Lending (Regulation Z) governing use of digital user accounts to access Buy Now, Pay Later loans. Credit unions are Regulation Z creditors, and America's Credit Unions filed its own comment letter on this exact rule (letter 1126, 'Comment Letter to CFPB on BNPL Digital User Accounts', 2024-07-31), which ACU classifies under its Consumer Protection issue area -- establishing the credit-union policy nexus and placing the measure in the outline's Consumer Protection section, not Payment & Technology. The legacy 'Payments' category is unsupported: the north-star Payments boundary is real-time payments, FedNow, instant payment fraud, payment system access, ACH payment, faster payments and payment stablecoin, none of which a Regulation Z consumer-credit rule touches; the legacy retrieval URL shows the measure was pulled in by a legacy Payments query containing a loose 'buy now pay later' term that the outline-derived Payments query does not carry. Discovery's own routing of CFPB rule disapprovals by the rule's subject (Regulation Z credit card penalty fees -> credit_card_consumer_fee_mandates at 118:hjres:121 and 118:sjres:70) and ACU's parallel disapproval letters (396, 1581) fix the corrected categories. Operative text was not reviewed: no BillStatus receipt, GovInfo object or discovery record for this key is held locally.

official_title: Expressing support for the designation of the week of September 13, 2021, through September 17, 2021, as "National Small Business Week" to celebrate the contributions of small businesses and entrepreneurs in every community in the United States.
reason: The official CRS summary states the measure's complete operative content: the resolution celebrates the contributions of small businesses and supports the designation of National Small Business Week, and supports efforts to provide small businesses with aid and assistance through certain programs and initiatives. A simple House resolution expressing support for a commemorative designation carries no operative policy effect on any regulated institution, so it cannot fall inside any of the nineteen policy categories; in particular it touches none of the member-business-lending identifiers, every one of which is credit-union or MBL specific. This is affirmative official evidence of falling outside the nineteen categories rather than mere absence from discovery. It is also the largest scoring artifact in this group: the two National Small Business Week resolutions together account for 93 selected member-bill contributions in the live archive under Member Business Lending. Independent prior art agrees: the 2026-07-24 legislative audit named these two resolutions among the bills with no credit-union nexus on their face, a finding that survived adversarial review, though that audit is corroborating prior art and the exclusion here rests on the official CRS summary.
